<reason>A won a competitive debate by a clearer motion reading and better comparative weighing. B landed a live scarcity story—restriction often deletes mixed placements rather than converting them, and A admitted deletion—but A made the clash easier to decide: unpaid “open” slots are already rationed by who can work for free, so volume is not access. A’s dilemma (valuable labor vs genuine education) and crystallization of B’s “only makes sense unpaid” line outpointed B’s grey-middle/line-drawing worry.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s R1 dilemma ([A2.1]) and later use of B’s concession that the package “only makes sense if cash is not also required,” turning mixed-value internships into a family-funded wage subsidy rather than a first look.</best_rebuttal>
